title: He Turned $400 Into $2.5M Using AI (No Coding)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: John Cheney promotes Gen AIPI, his own company. He also says Replit gave him free credits after he offered to keep talking about it. The $22,000 app claim is relayed from an email, with the app details withheld.

stated_problem.quote: I was like man they are going to miss out and I need to do something about it.

idea.name: Gen AIPI AI training and implementation
idea.one_liner: Helps companies assess employee AI readiness, train staff, and install and manage AI systems for project fees and ongoing retainers.
idea.customer: Business owners and CEOs, especially companies without a CTO; he says most customers average about $30 million in revenue.
idea.offer: Started with an AI readiness test, self-paced courses, and certification; expanded to employee assessment, training, AI strategy, transformation, and ongoing system installation and management.
idea.revenue_model: B2B project fees and monthly retainers; the original funnel also offered paid courses and a certification test.

acquisition_channels.details: He says he called businesses and recommends researching prospects, finding CEO phone numbers, and calling.
He posted progress on LinkedIn and recommended posting on personal Facebook and LinkedIn.
He says many later deals came through referrals.
He messaged people he knew who owned companies; the messaging medium is not specified.
He planned to run ads for the original AI test, but says he did not put further advertising behind it after pivoting.

ideas.delivery: Initially an online readiness test with self-paced courses and certification. The business pivoted to employee assessments, workshops and training, AI strategy, and ongoing system installation and management, delivered by John and later his team.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK outreach, screen cold calls against TPS/CTPS; cold email is limited to corporate subscribers with an opt-out. The transcript mentions messaging company owners but not the medium or their legal form, so avoid unsolicited SMS, WhatsApp, or social DMs to individual subscribers or sole traders. UK GDPR applies to sourced contact data and employee assessment data; consumer course sales must follow consumer rules, and any consumer subscription could engage DMCC Act subscription requirements.
